# Pinned extractor runtime - keep in lockstep with .github/workflows/ci.yml.
# Providers are pure subprocesses; this is their entire dependency surface.
#
# HASH-PINNED, and installed with `pip install --require-hashes`. Exact versions
# are not a supply-chain control: pip executes package build and install code,
# and `pip install -r` runs on every consumer's CI runner (action.yml), on the
# rollup runner, and in release.yml - which holds `id-token: write` for the
# provenance attestation. A compromised or re-uploaded artifact at a pinned
# version would execute there. R9's "zero install scripts" was only ever true of
# the npm half; this closes the other half.
#
# Every sha256 published for each version is listed, so all three CI operating
# systems and every supported Python resolve to a wheel that is covered. The
# dependency closure is exactly these eight - none of them declares a runtime
# dependency - so --require-hashes has nothing unpinned to trip over.
#
# To bump: change the version, then regenerate with
#   scripts/dev/hash-requirements.py
# Never hand-edit a hash.
